analysis: The code snippet defines a method `blockForPending` that synchronously retrieves results from pending futures in a loop. Prior to calling `f.get()`, no validation is performed on the state of the future (e.g., whether it is cancelled). After the call, `InterruptedException` and `ExecutionException` are caught and rethrown as runtime exceptions via `Log.errRTExcept`. The API documentation for `get` declares three exceptions: `CancellationException` (unchecked), `ExecutionException` (checked), and `InterruptedException` (checked). The code explicitly catches the two checked exceptions, thereby avoiding their propagation. However, `CancellationException` is not caught and no pre-check (e.g., `isCancelled()`) prevents its occurrence. Therefore, `CancellationException` can still be thrown and is not avoided.
remark: The `CancellationException` will be thrown if any of the pending futures have been cancelled. Since the loop calls `f.get()` without checking whether the future was cancelled (e.g., via `f.isCancelled()`), the exception can propagate uncaught out of the `blockForPending` method.
